review_notes: Reviewed the complete target file, the definitions of residueTestMean, quadraticResidueTest, and logPrimeBand, and the downstream use in BiasedPrimeBlock. I found one concrete membership-simplification improvement; no other simp-interface issue was sufficiently supported.

findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def biasedPrimeBand (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) (T δ : ℝ) (t : ℕ → ℤ) : Finset ℕ :=
  (logPrimeBand T).filter fun p => δ ≤ |residueTestMean (tailSupport A N p) (quadraticResidueTest p (t p))|
findings.problem: The definition has no named simp lemma for membership. Consequently, a downstream consumer extracts the bias condition by applying the generic filter-membership equivalence directly, rather than simplifying membership in the named set.
findings.proposed_change: Add a membership theorem tagged `[simp]`, for example `@[simp] theorem mem_biasedPrimeBand ... : p ∈ biasedPrimeBand A N T δ t ↔ p ∈ logPrimeBand T ∧ δ ≤ |residueTestMean (tailSupport A N p) (quadraticResidueTest p (t p))| := by simp [biasedPrimeBand]`. This orients rewriting from membership in the named set to its filter conditions, without rewriting those conditions back into the set.
findings.benefit: The membership normal form exposes both the band condition and the bias condition to `simp`, giving downstream proofs a direct, stable interface instead of requiring `Finset.mem_filter.mp`. The right-hand side does not contain `biasedPrimeBand`, so this orientation does not introduce a rewrite cycle.
